newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand's PTT gets nod to invest in Burma gas.
newsitem.headline: Thailand's PTT gets nod to invest in Burma gas.

text.p: Thailand's state-run Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) on Wednesday got the green light to invest in a natural gas project in Burma in which Texaco is also a partner, a senior minister said.

Sompong Amornvivat, a minister in the prime minister's office, said the Board of National Energy Policy Office approved PTT's plan to invest and buy natural from Burma's Yetagun project in the Andaman Sea.
It also allowed the agency to sign a contract to buy natural gas from the Nam Pong and Benchamas fields, he said but did not give details.
The PTT plans to invest in the Yentagun project through its exploration arm PTT Exploration and Production Plc.
PTTEP late last month signed a farm-in agreement to develop and produce natural gas at the Yetagun project. It will hold 14.17 percent stake in the investment.
Other partners included Texaco Exploration Myanmar, Premier Petroleum Myanmar Co and Nippon Oil Exploration (Burma), a unit of Nippon Oil.

Yetagun field, located in the Gulf of Martaban in the Andaman Sea, has estimated natural gas reserves of around 1.1 trillion cubic feet. It is expected to come onstream in 1999 with initial capacity of 200 million cubic feet per day of natural gas.
